KUJO 02 / The accountability problem 2 / 18 Software production is outpacing verification. Agents can report completion. Teams still need a reviewable chain from requested work to release decision. 01 The claim “Tests passed. Ready to merge.” An illustrative agent statement. 02 The evidence Command, exit code, changed revision, environment and retained failure output. 03 The gap Useful logs already exist. Connecting them across tools and review boundaries remains work. Evidence & investor appendix ↗ KUJO / Investor briefing Thesis · existing agent controls acknowledged 2 2 Software production is outpacing verification.

KUJO 03 / Structural shift 3 / 18 Greater autonomy requires stronger accountability. The cost of an unverified action grows as agents gain authority. 01 Suggest code Human selects the change → diff review 02 Complete a task Agent edits and runs commands → execution records 03 Operate a workflow Retries and external effects → boundaries, recovery and approval Evidence & investor appendix ↗ KUJO / Investor briefing Conceptual progression; not a measured adoption curve 3 3 Greater autonomy requires stronger accountability.

KUJO 04 / Why now 4 / 18 AI use is broad. Trust remains conditional. Adoption of AI assistance is not evidence of autonomous production deployment. use coding assistants or coding agents at work 65.9% use AI agents or automated workflows at work 26.2% trust AI when answers are easy to validate 48% Evidence & investor appendix ↗ KUJO / Investor briefing M03–M04 · Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2026 4 4 AI use is broad. Trust remains conditional.

KUJO 05 / The Kujo system 5 / 18 Build with clarity. Operate with control. The language is the long-term foundation. Existing tools offer an earlier route into engineering workflows. 01 Clarity Kujo language / Spec / Eval: explicit intent and testable outcomes. 02 Context MCP / CaseFile / RunLedger: useful inputs, debugging evidence and run records. 03 Control Dispatch / Workcell / ShipCheck: orchestration, bounded execution and release checks. Existing repositories + coding agents explicit component contracts Kujo runtime + CLI Inspect the execution boundary Workcell owns supported container bounds. Dispatch owns workflow state. Neither confers enterprise certification. Inspect the evidence boundary CaseFile captures commands. Eval runs configured checks. RunLedger stores supplied outcomes. Artifacts remain separate. Evidence & investor appendix ↗ KUJO / Investor briefing T01–T14 · tool boundaries remain distinct 5 5 Build with clarity. Operate with control.

KUJO 06 / Lifecycle 6 / 18 Accountability spans the whole task. Each component owns a specific responsibility. A reviewable workflow composes their artifacts explicitly. 01 Instruction → Context Spec / PackWrite → MCP and repository context 02 Execution → Evaluation Dispatch / Workcell → Eval result artifacts 03 Evidence → Review → Release CaseFile / RunLedger → reviewer → ShipCheck gate Human authority remains explicit at the release decision. Evidence & investor appendix ↗ KUJO / Investor briefing Composition map; not automatic end-to-end enforcement 6 6 Accountability spans the whole task.

KUJO 07 / Engineering proof 7 / 18 The foundation is already being built. Inspect the implementation and its limits, then reproduce the smallest useful proof. 01 Language and VM Kujo 1.9.0 is documented; a local 1.9.0 binary executes the recorded fixture tooling. 02 Bounded execution Workcell 1.3 documents Docker/Podman limits, explicit exports and receipt verification. 03 Reviewable artifact This presentation uses the native Kujo builder. Its demo retains a failing command, correction and evaluation. Evidence & investor appendix ↗ KUJO / Investor briefing T01, T03, T08, T14 · release documentation ≠ all HEAD features 7 7 The foundation is already being built.

KUJO 08 / Recorded demonstration 8 / 18 A claim becomes inspectable evidence. Recorded local coding fixture: correct a post-money ownership calculation. Inspect what failed, what changed and what passed. 01 Request Return 20% for $6M raised at $30M post-money. 02 Execution CaseFile captures real Node assertion failure and corrected execution. 03 Decision Eval checks the correction. Accept this fixture; no production release. Inspect the correction − raise / (postMoney + raise) * 100
+ raise / postMoney * 100 Open failure, commands & evaluation → Evidence & investor appendix ↗ KUJO / Investor briefing Assistant-authored seeded fixture · CaseFile + Eval · local host 8 8 A claim becomes inspectable evidence.

KUJO 09 / Adoption without migration 9 / 18 Adopt the ecosystem before the language. Keep application code in its existing language. Introduce accountability at the workflow boundary. 01 Today: wrap the task Use CaseFile for command evidence and Eval for explicit repository checks. 02 Then: control execution Adopt Dispatch or Workcell after validating the target environment and runtime pins. 03 Over time: go deeper Choose Kujo for new agent tooling where native language integration adds value. Evidence & investor appendix ↗ KUJO / Investor briefing T02–T04, T08 · tools have their own runtime dependencies 9 9 Adopt the ecosystem before the language.

KUJO 10 / Initial customer 10 / 18 Start with teams already delegating engineering work. Proposed beachhead: agent-platform builders shipping repeatable engineering workflows. 01 Buyer / user Platform engineering lead / engineers operating coding-agent harnesses. 02 Immediate pain Failed runs are expensive to reconstruct. Review spans commits, logs and agent transcripts. 03 Purchase hypothesis Pay for retained evidence, controlled execution and team review if they reduce investigation time. Evidence & investor appendix ↗ KUJO / Investor briefing Proposed segment; no customer interviews or demand validation 10 10 Start with teams already delegating engineering work.

KUJO 11 / Business model 11 / 18 Open tooling can lead to a commercial operating layer. Earn developer trust through useful local tools. Charge for shared operational responsibilities. 01 Available foundation Open repositories and local developer tooling. 02 Proposed team service Hosted evidence, retention, shared review and execution capacity. 03 Proposed enterprise tier Organization policy, deployment controls, support and governance. Evidence & investor appendix ↗ KUJO / Investor briefing Hosted offerings and pricing are proposals, not available SKUs 11 11 Open tooling can lead to a commercial operating layer.

KUJO 12 / Market model 12 / 18 A focused entry market can support a meaningful business. Illustrative bottom-up model. Organization counts and annual contracts are assumptions to validate. initial target organizations × $24K ACV 2,000 illustrative annual serviceable revenue pool $48M 100 customers × $24K; milestone scenario, not forecast $2.4M Evidence & investor appendix ↗ KUJO / Investor briefing Planning only · editable assumptions in appendix 12 12 A focused entry market can support a meaningful business.

KUJO 13 / Position and defensibility 13 / 18 Accountability requires more than generating code. Existing platforms are strong. Kujo must win on useful evidence and the cost of operating reliable workflows. 01 Coding agents / GitHub Generation, repository context and review are already integrated into major developer surfaces. 02 Orchestration / LangGraph Persistence, recovery and human review are established capabilities. 03 Kujo opportunity Connect explicit contracts, bounded work and inspectable artifacts. Prove adoption before claiming a moat. Evidence & investor appendix ↗ KUJO / Investor briefing C01–C02, T01–T14 · no exclusivity or benchmark superiority 13 13 Accountability requires more than generating code.

KUJO 14 / Distribution 14 / 18 Meet developers inside their existing workflows. The planned December 2026 open-source campaign should produce repeat usage and customer learning. 01 Discovery GitHub releases, technical demos, docs and reproducible fixtures → qualified visits. 02 Activation Agent harness recipes and MCP tooling → first successful evidence run. 03 Retention → revenue Repeat weekly runs → design-partner discussions → paid pilots and renewal evidence. Evidence & investor appendix ↗ KUJO / Investor briefing Campaign and partnerships planned; measure cohorts, not raw impressions 14 14 Meet developers inside their existing workflows.

KUJO 15 / Momentum 15 / 18 Execution is visible. Demand still needs proof. Engineering output, external adoption and commercial traction are different measures. 01 Engineering output Public repositories, documented releases and the locally reproduced evidence fixture. 02 External adoption Verified outside usage, retention and independent integrations: data not supplied. 03 Commercial traction Design partners, paying customers and revenue: data not supplied. Complete before investor distribution. Evidence & investor appendix ↗ KUJO / Investor briefing Unavailable is not zero; no invented traction 15 15 Execution is visible. Demand still needs proof.

KUJO 16 / Founder and team 16 / 18 Built through sustained open-source engineering. Robert DeVore connects open-web product work with a growing language and developer-tooling ecosystem. 01 Background Public biography describes years of WordPress, WooCommerce, plugins and publishing systems. 02 Current work Language/runtime infrastructure, orchestration, evaluation, telemetry and evidence workflows. 03 Team enabled by capital Proposed hires in runtime, execution reliability and developer experience; later customer engineering. Evidence & investor appendix ↗ KUJO / Investor briefing F01 · first-person source; no invented tenure, team or security credentials 16 16 Built through sustained open-source engineering.

KUJO 17 / Investment and milestones 17 / 18 Capital turns a technical foundation into an adopted platform. Working seed scenario. Financing terms and hiring pace remain assumptions. target raise $6M post-money valuation or SAFE cap assumption $30M planned runway, including reserve 24 mo 0–6 mo Flagship evidence workflow 6–12 mo External validation + pilots 12–24 mo Paid retention + repeatability Evidence & investor appendix ↗ KUJO / Investor briefing 20% simplified ownership before further dilution · $150K founder annual base 17 17 Capital turns a technical foundation into an adopted platform.

KUJO 18 / The vision 18 / 18 Agents will build more software. The organizations deploying it will still be accountable for what it does. KUJO Trust at the speed of AI.
